children: Oil prices continue to fall in early Asian trade after declining over 8% overnight on rising hopes for an end to the Middle East conflict following the Democrats' sweep in the U.S. midterm elections. Still, ANZ analysts think the market reaction is unwarranted as there are risks of escalation in the conflict after the elections. "There appears no end in sight to Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz, which has constrained oil flow," they note. Exports of crude oil from the Persian Gulf averaged 17.1 million barrels a day in October, according to ship-tracking data, down from September, they say. Front-month WTI crude-oil futures are down 0.4% at $87.77 a barrel, while front-month Brent is 0.2% lower at $94.64 a barrel. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
